problem_description.description: Alice and Bob have decided to play the game "Rock, Paper, Scissors". The game consists of several rounds, each round is independent of each other. In each round, both players show one of the following things at the same time: rock, paper or scissors. If both players showed the same things then the round outcome is a draw. Otherwise, the following rules applied:  if one player showed rock and the other one showed scissors, then the player who showed rock is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser;  if one player showed scissors and the other one showed paper, then the player who showed scissors is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser;  if one player showed paper and the other one showed rock, then the player who showed paper is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser. Alice and Bob decided to play exactly $$$n$$$ rounds of the game described above. Alice decided to show rock $$$a_1$$$ times, show scissors $$$a_2$$$ times and show paper $$$a_3$$$ times. Bob decided to show rock $$$b_1$$$ times, show scissors $$$b_2$$$ times and show paper $$$b_3$$$ times. Though, both Alice and Bob did not choose the sequence in which they show things. It is guaranteed that $$$a_1 + a_2 + a_3 = n$$$ and $$$b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = n$$$.Your task is to find two numbers:  the minimum number of round Alice can win;  the maximum number of rounds Alice can win.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^{9}$$$) — the number of rounds. The second line of the input contains three integers $$$a_1, a_2, a_3$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the number of times Alice will show rock, scissors and paper, respectively. It is guaranteed that $$$a_1 + a_2 + a_3 = n$$$. The third line of the input contains three integers $$$b_1, b_2, b_3$$$ ($$$0 \le b_j \le n$$$) — the number of times Bob will show rock, scissors and paper, respectively. It is guaranteed that $$$b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = n$$$.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two integers: the minimum and the maximum number of rounds Alice can win.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first example, Alice will not win any rounds if she shows scissors and then paper and Bob shows rock and then scissors. In the best outcome, Alice will win one round if she shows paper and then scissors, and Bob shows rock and then scissors.In the second example, Alice will not win any rounds if Bob shows the same things as Alice each round.In the third example, Alice always shows paper and Bob always shows rock so Alice will win all three rounds anyway.

import heapq

class mcf_graph_int_cost:

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.pos = []
        self.g = [[] for _ in range(n)]


    def add_edge(self, from_, to, cap, cost):
        # assert 0 <= from_ < self.n
        # assert 0 <= to < self.n
        m = len(self.pos)
        self.pos.append((from_, len(self.g[from_])))
        self.g[from_].append(self.__class__._edge(to, len(self.g[to]), cap, cost))
        self.g[to].append(self.__class__._edge(from_, len(self.g[from_]) - 1, 0, -cost))
        return m


    class edge:
        def __init__(self, from_, to, cap, flow, cost):
            self.from_ = from_
            self.to = to
            self.cap = cap
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost


    def get_edge(self, i):
        _e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
        _re = self.g[_e.to][_e.rev]
        return self.__class__.edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost)


    def edges(self):
        ret = []
        for i in range(len(self.pos)):
            _e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
            _re = self.g[_e.to][_e.rev]
            ret.append(self.__class__.edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost))
        return ret


    def _dual_ref(self, s, t):
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.vis = [False] * self.n

        que = [s] # s ==  (0 << 32) + s 
        self.dist[s] = 0
        while que:
            v = heapq.heappop(que) & 4294967295
            if self.vis[v]:
                continue
            self.vis[v] = True
            if v == t:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.g[v])):
                e = self.g[v][i]
                if self.vis[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                    continue
                cost = e.cost - self.dual[e.to] + self.dual[v]
                if self.dist[e.to] > self.dist[v] + cost:
                    self.dist[e.to] = self.dist[v] + cost
                    self.pv[e.to] = v
                    self.pe[e.to] = i
                    heapq.heappush(que, ((self.dist[e.to] << 32) + e.to))
        if not self.vis[t]:
            return False

        for v in range(self.n):
            if not self.vis[v]:
                continue
            self.dual[v] -= self.dist[t] - self.dist[v]
        
        return True


    def slope(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        # assert 0 <= s < self.n
        # assert 0 <= t < self.n
        # assert s != t
        
        self.dual = [0] * self.n
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.vis = [False] * self.n
        
        flow = 0
        cost = 0
        prev_cost = -1
        result = [(flow, cost)]
        while flow < flow_limit:
            if not self._dual_ref(s, t):
                break
            c = flow_limit - flow
            v = t
            while v != s:
                c = min(c, self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]].cap)
                v = self.pv[v]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                e = self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]]
                e.cap -= c
                self.g[v][e.rev].cap += c
                v = self.pv[v]
            d = -self.dual[s]
            flow += c
            cost += c * d
            if prev_cost == d:
                result.pop()
            result.append((flow, cost))
            prev_cost = cost
        return result


    def flow(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        return self.slope(s, t, flow_limit)[-1]

    
    class _edge:
        def __init__(self, to, rev, cap, cost):
            self.to = to
            self.rev = rev
            self.cap = cap
            self.cost = cost

import heapq

class MCFGraph:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.pos = []
        self.graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def add_edge(self, from_, to, cap, cost):
        m = len(self.pos)
        self.pos.append((from_, len(self.graph[from_])))
        self.graph[from_].append(self._Edge(to, len(self.graph[to]), cap, cost))
        self.graph[to].append(self._Edge(from_, len(self.graph[from_]) - 1, 0, -cost))
        return m

    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, from_, to, cap, flow, cost):
            self.from_ = from_
            self.to = to
            self.cap = cap
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost

    def get_edge(self, i):
        _e = self.graph[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
        _re = self.graph[_e.to][_e.rev]
        return self.Edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost)

    def edges(self):
        ret = []
        for i in range(len(self.pos)):
            _e = self.graph[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
            _re = self.graph[_e.to][_e.rev]
            ret.append(self.Edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost))
        return ret

    def _dual_ref(self, s, t):
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.visited = [False] * self.n
        que = [s]
        self.dist[s] = 0
        while que:
            v = heapq.heappop(que) & 4294967295
            if self.visited[v]:
                continue
            self.visited[v] = True
            if v == t:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.graph[v])):
                e = self.graph[v][i]
                if self.visited[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                    continue
                reduced_cost = e.cost - self.dual[e.to] + self.dual[v]
                if self.dist[e.to] > self.dist[v] + reduced_cost:
                    self.dist[e.to] = self.dist[v] + reduced_cost
                    self.pv[e.to] = v
                    self.pe[e.to] = i
                    heapq.heappush(que, ((self.dist[e.to] << 32) + e.to))
        if not self.visited[t]:
            return False
        for v in range(self.n):
            if not self.visited[v]:
                continue
            self.dual[v] -= self.dist[t] - self.dist[v]
        return True

    def slope(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        self.dual = [0] * self.n
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.visited = [False] * self.n
        flow = 0
        total_cost = 0
        prev_reduced_cost = -1
        result = [(flow, total_cost)]
        while flow < flow_limit:
            if not self._dual_ref(s, t):
                break
            c = flow_limit - flow
            v = t
            while v != s:
                c = min(c, self.graph[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]].cap)
                v = self.pv[v]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                e = self.graph[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]]
                e.cap -= c
                self.graph[v][e.rev].cap += c
                v = self.pv[v]
            d = -self.dual[s]
            flow += c
            total_cost += c * d
            if prev_reduced_cost == d:
                result.pop()
            result.append((flow, total_cost))
            prev_reduced_cost = d
        return result

    def flow(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        return self.slope(s, t, flow_limit)[-1]

    class _Edge:
        def __init__(self, to, rev, cap, cost):
            self.to = to
            self.rev = rev
            self.cap = cap
            self.cost = cost

import heapq

class MinimumCostFlow:
    def __init__(self, node_count):
        self.size = node_count
        self.edges_info = []
        self.adjacency = [[] for _ in range(node_count)]

    def connect(self, src, dst, capacity, weight):
        idx = len(self.edges_info)
        self.edges_info.append((src, len(self.adjacency[src])))
        self.adjacency[src].append(self.Edge(dst, len(self.adjacency[dst]), capacity, weight))
        self.adjacency[dst].append(self.Edge(src, len(self.adjacency[src]) - 1, 0, -weight))
        return idx

    class Link:
        def __init__(self, origin, destination, capacity, flow, weight):
            self.origin = origin
            self.destination = destination
            self.capacity = capacity
            self.flow = flow
            self.weight = weight

    def retrieve_link(self, index):
        source, pos = self.edges_info[index]
        forward = self.adjacency[source][pos]
        backward = self.adjacency[forward.destination][forward.rev]
        return self.Link(source, forward.destination, forward.capacity + backward.capacity, backward.capacity, forward.weight)

    def all_links(self):
        output = []
        for idx in range(len(self.edges_info)):
            source, pos = self.edges_info[idx]
            forward = self.adjacency[source][pos]
            backward = self.adjacency[forward.destination][forward.rev]
            output.append(self.Link(source, forward.destination, forward.capacity + backward.capacity, backward.capacity, forward.weight))
        return output

    def _potential_update(self, source, target):
        self.distances = [4294967295] * self.size
        self.parents = [-1] * self.size
        self.parent_edges = [-1] * self.size
        self.marked = [False] * self.size
        queue = [source]
        self.distances[source] = 0
        while queue:
            current = heapq.heappop(queue) & 4294967295
            if self.marked[current]:
                continue
            self.marked[current] = True
            if current == target:
                break
            for idx in range(len(self.adjacency[current])):
                edge = self.adjacency[current][idx]
                if self.marked[edge.destination] or edge.capacity == 0:
                    continue
                adjusted_cost = edge.weight - self.potential[edge.destination] + self.potential[current]
                if self.distances[edge.destination] > self.distances[current] + adjusted_cost:
                    self.distances[edge.destination] = self.distances[current] + adjusted_cost
                    self.parents[edge.destination] = current
                    self.parent_edges[edge.destination] = idx
                    heapq.heappush(queue, ((self.distances[edge.destination] << 32) + edge.destination))
        if not self.marked[target]:
            return False
        for node in range(self.size):
            if not self.marked[node]:
                continue
            self.potential[node] -= self.distances[target] - self.distances[node]
        return True

    def pareto_frontier(self, source, target, max_flow=4294967295):
        self.potential = [0] * self.size
        self.distances = [4294967295] * self.size
        self.parents = [-1] * self.size
        self.parent_edges = [-1] * self.size
        self.marked = [False] * self.size
        current_flow = 0
        total_weight = 0
        last_weight = -1
        frontier = [(current_flow, total_weight)]
        while current_flow < max_flow:
            if not self._potential_update(source, target):
                break
            bottleneck = max_flow - current_flow
            node = target
            while node != source:
                bottleneck = min(bottleneck, self.adjacency[self.parents[node]][self.parent_edges[node]].capacity)
                node = self.parents[node]
            node = target
            while node != source:
                edge = self.adjacency[self.parents[node]][self.parent_edges[node]]
                edge.capacity -= bottleneck
                self.adjacency[node][edge.rev].capacity += bottleneck
                node = self.parents[node]
            reduced_cost = -self.potential[source]
            current_flow += bottleneck
            total_weight += bottleneck * reduced_cost
            if last_weight == reduced_cost:
                frontier.pop()
            frontier.append((current_flow, total_weight))
            last_weight = reduced_cost
        return frontier

    def min_cost_flow(self, source, target, max_flow=4294967295):
        return self.pareto_frontier(source, target, max_flow)[-1]

    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, destination, reverse, capacity, weight):
            self.destination = destination
            self.reverse = reverse
            self.capacity = capacity
            self.weight = weight

import heapq

class Graph:
    def __init__(self, size):
        self.N = size
        self.edge_list = []
        self.adj = [[] for _ in range(size)]

    def add(self, u, v, cap, w):
        idx = len(self.edge_list)
        self.edge_list.append((u, len(self.adj[u])))
        self.adj[u].append(self._Edge(v, len(self.adj[v]), cap, w))
        self.adj[v].append(self._Edge(u, len(self.adj[u]) - 1, 0, -w))
        return idx

    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, src, dst, cap, flow, cost):
            self.src = src
            self.dst = dst
            self.cap = cap
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost

    def get(self, i):
        u, pos = self.edge_list[i]
        f = self.adj[u][pos]
        r = self.adj[f.dst][f.rev]
        return self.Edge(u, f.dst, f.cap + r.cap, r.cap, f.cost)

    def list_edges(self):
        res = []
        for i in range(len(self.edge_list)):
            u, pos = self.edge_list[i]
            f = self.adj[u][pos]
            r = self.adj[f.dst][f.rev]
            res.append(self.Edge(u, f.dst, f.cap + r.cap, r.cap, f.cost))
        return res

    def _refine(self, s, t):
        self.d = [4294967295] * self.N
        self.par = [-1] * self.N
        self.par_edge = [-1] * self.N
        self.seen = [False] * self.N
        heap = [s]
        self.d[s] = 0
        while heap:
            v = heapq.heappop(heap) & 4294967295
            if self.seen[v]:
                continue
            self.seen[v] = True
            if v == t:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.adj[v])):
                e = self.adj[v][i]
                if self.seen[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                    continue
                rc = e.cost - self.phi[e.to] + self.phi[v]
                if self.d[e.to] > self.d[v] + rc:
                    self.d[e.to] = self.d[v] + rc
                    self.par[e.to] = v
                    self.par_edge[e.to] = i
                    heapq.heappush(heap, ((self.d[e.to] << 32) + e.to))
        if not self.seen[t]:
            return False
        for i in range(self.N):
            if not self.seen[i]:
                continue
            self.phi[i] -= self.d[t] - self.d[i]
        return True

    def frontier(self, s, t, limit=4294967295):
        self.phi = [0] * self.N
        self.d = [4294967295] * self.N
        self.par = [-1] * self.N
        self.par_edge = [-1] * self.N
        self.seen = [False] * self.N
        flow = 0
        cost = 0
        last_cost = -1
        points = [(flow, cost)]
        while flow < limit:
            if not self._refine(s, t):
                break
            c = limit - flow
            v = t
            while v != s:
                c = min(c, self.adj[self.par[v]][self.par_edge[v]].cap)
                v = self.par[v]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                e = self.adj[self.par[v]][self.par_edge[v]]
                e.cap -= c
                self.adj[v][e.rev].cap += c
                v = self.par[v]
            d = -self.phi[s]
            flow += c
            cost += c * d
            if last_cost == d:
                points.pop()
            points.append((flow, cost))
            last_cost = d
        return points

    def send(self, s, t, limit=4294967295):
        return self.frontier(s, t, limit)[-1]

    class _Edge:
        def __init__(self, to, rev, cap, cost):
            self.to = to
            self.rev = rev
            self.cap = cap
            self.cost = cost

import heapq

class NetworkFlow:
    def __init__(self, nodes):
        self.V = nodes
        self.edges_descriptor = []
        self.adj_list = [[] for _ in range(nodes)]

    def link(self, u, v, capacity, cost):
        idx = len(self.edges_descriptor)
        self.edges_descriptor.append((u, len(self.adj_list[u])))
        self.adj_list[u].append(self._Link(v, len(self.adj_list[v]), capacity, cost))
        self.adj_list[v].append(self._Link(u, len(self.adj_list[u]) - 1, 0, -cost))
        return idx

    class Connection:
        def __init__(self, start, end, capacity, flow, cost):
            self.start = start
            self.end = end
            self.capacity = capacity
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost

    def fetch(self, i):
        u, pos = self.edges_descriptor[i]
        fwd = self.adj_list[u][pos]
        bwd = self.adj_list[fwd.to][fwd.rev]
        return self.Connection(u, fwd.to, fwd.cap + bwd.cap, bwd.cap, fwd.cost)

    def enumerate(self):
        out = []
        for i in range(len(self.edges_descriptor)):
            u, pos = self.edges_descriptor[i]
            fwd = self.adj_list[u][pos]
            bwd = self.adj_list[fwd.to][fwd.rev]
            out.append(self.Connection(u, fwd.to, fwd.cap + bwd.cap, bwd.cap, fwd.cost))
        return out

    def _adjust(self, src, dst):
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.V
        self.parent = [-1] * self.V
        self.parent_edge = [-1] * self.V
        self.in_queue = [False] * self.V
        heap = [src]
        self.dist[src] = 0
        while heap:
            v = heapq.heappop(heap) & 4294967295
            if self.in_queue[v]:
                continue
            self.in_queue[v] = True
            if v == dst:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.adj_list[v])):
                e = self.adj_list[v][i]
                if self.in_queue[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                    continue
                rc = e.cost - self.potential[e.to] + self.potential[v]
                if self.dist[e.to] > self.dist[v] + rc:
                    self.dist[e.to] = self.dist[v] + rc
                    self.parent[e.to] = v
                    self.parent_edge[e.to] = i
                    heapq.heappush(heap, ((self.dist[e.to] << 32) + e.to))
        if not self.in_queue[dst]:
            return False
        for i in range(self.V):
            if not self.in_queue[i]:
                continue
            self.potential[i] -= self.dist[dst] - self.dist[i]
        return True

    def trade(self, src, dst, cap_limit=4294967295):
        self.potential = [0] * self.V

            points.append((total_flow, total_cost))
            prev_cost = d

    def push(self, src, dst, cap_limit=4294967295):

import heapq

class FlowNetwork:
    def __init__(self, vertex_count):
        self.V = vertex_count
        self.edge_indices = []
        self.adj = [[] for _ in range(vertex_count)]

    def add_edge(self, u, v, capacity, cost):
        idx = len(self.edge_indices)
        self.edge_indices.append((u, len(self.adj[u])))
        self.adj[u].append(self._Link(v, len(self.adj[v]), capacity, cost))
        self.adj[v].append(self._Link(u, len(self.adj[u]) - 1, 0, -cost))
        return idx

    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, source, target, capacity, flow, cost):
            self.source = source
            self.target = target
            self.capacity = capacity
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost

    def get_edge(self, i):
        u, pos = self.edge_indices[i]
        forward = self.adj[u][pos]
        backward = self.adj[forward.target][forward.rev]
        return self.Edge(u, forward.target, forward.capacity + backward.capacity, backward.capacity, forward.cost)

    def list_edges(self):
        result = []
        for i in range(len(self.edge_indices)):
            u, pos = self.edge_indices[i]
            forward = self.adj[u][pos]
            backward = self.adj[forward.target][forward.rev]
            result.append(self.Edge(u, forward.target, forward.capacity + backward.capacity, backward.capacity, forward.cost))
        return result

    def _reweight(self, source, sink):
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.V
        self.parent = [-1] * self.V
        self.parent_edge_index = [-1] * self.V
        self.in_spt = [False] * self.V
        heap = [source]
        self.dist[source] = 0
        while heap:
            v = heapq.heappop(heap) & 4294967295
            if self.in_spt[v]:
                continue
            self.in_spt[v] = True
            if v == sink:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.adj[v])):
                e = self.adj[v][i]
                if self.in_spt[e.target] or e.capacity == 0:
                    continue
                reduced_cost = e.cost - self.potential[e.target] + self.potential[v]
                if self.dist[e.target] > self.dist[v] + reduced_cost:
                    self.dist[e.target] = self.dist[v] + reduced_cost
                    self.parent[e.target] = v
                    self.parent_edge_index[e.target] = i
                    heapq.heappush(heap, ((self.dist[e.target] << 32) + e.target))
        if not self.in_spt[sink]:
            return False
        for i in range(self.V):
            if not self.in_spt[i]:
                continue
            self.potential[i] -= self.dist[sink] - self.dist[i]
        return True

    def pareto(self, source, sink, flow_cap=4294967295):
        self.potential = [0] * self.V
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.V
        self.parent = [-1] * self.V
        self.parent_edge_index = [-1] * self.V
        self.in_spt = [False] * self.V
        total_flow = 0
        total_cost = 0
        last_cost = -1
        points = [(total_flow, total_cost)]
        while total_flow < flow_cap:
            if not self._reweight(source, sink):
                break
            bottleneck = flow_cap - total_flow
            node = sink
            while node != source:
                bottleneck = min(bottleneck, self.adj[self.parent[node]][self.parent_edge_index[node]].capacity)
                node = self.parent[node]
            node = sink
            while node != source:
                e = self.adj[self.parent[node]][self.parent_edge_index[node]]
                e.capacity -= bottleneck
                self.adj[node][e.rev].capacity += bottleneck
                node = self.parent[node]
            d = -self.potential[source]
            total_flow += bottleneck
            total_cost += bottleneck * d
            if last_cost == d:
                points.pop()
            points.append((total_flow, total_cost))
            last_cost = d
        return points

    def max_flow_min_cost(self, source, sink, flow_cap=4294967295):
        return self.pareto(source, sink, flow_cap)[-1]

    class _Link:
        def __init__(self, target, rev, capacity, cost):
            self.target = target
            self.rev = rev
            self.capacity = capacity
            self.cost = cost

            b = os.read(self._fd, max(os.fstat(self._fd).st_size, BUFSIZE))

The player is initially standing at the root of the tree and the exit from the tree is located at some leaf node. Let's index all the leaf nodes from the left to the right from 1 to 2h. The exit is located at some node n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 2h, the player doesn't know where the exit is so he has to guess his way out!Amr follows simple algorithm to choose the path. Let's consider infinite command string "LRLRLRLRL..." (consisting of alternating characters 'L' and 'R'). Now Amr wonders, if he follows this algorithm, how many nodes he is going to visit before reaching the exit?

problem_description.notes: NoteA perfect binary tree of height h is a binary tree consisting of h + 1 levels. As a result, we get something like vasyaatgmaildotcom. Your task is to transform it into a proper email address (vasya@gmail.com). Also, a proper email address doesn't start with and doesn't end with an at sign. Moreover, an email address contains exactly one such symbol as @, yet may contain any number (possible, zero) of dots. You have to carry out a series of replacements so that the length of the result was as short as possible and it was a proper email address. If the lengths are equal, you should print the lexicographically minimal result. Overall, two variants of replacement are possible: dot can be replaced by a dot, at can be replaced by an at.

If there are several solutions to that problem, print the lexicographically minimal one (the lexicographical comparison of the lines are implemented with an operator < in modern programming languages). In the ASCII table the symbols go in this order: . @ ab...z

def convert(s):
    length = len(s)
    if s.startswith('dot') or s.startswith('at') or s.endswith('at') or s.endswith('dot'):
        # Handle case where starts with 'dot'
        if s.startswith('dot') and length > 2:
            rest = s[3:]
            parts = rest.split('dot')
            middle = '.'.join(parts)
            at_index = middle.find('at')
            if at_index != -1:
                new_mid = middle[:at_index] + '@' + middle[at_index+2:]
                modified = 'dot' + new_mid
                if modified and modified[-1] == '.':
                    return modified[:-1] + 'dot'
                elif modified and modified[-1] == '@':
                    return modified[:-1] + 'at'
                return modified
        
        # Handle case where starts with 'at'
        if s.startswith('at') and length > 1:
            rest = s[2:]
            parts = rest.split('dot')
            middle = '.'.join(parts)
            at_index = middle.find('at')
            if at_index != -1:
                new_mid = middle[:at_index] + '@' + middle[at_index+2:]
                modified = 'at' + new_mid
                if modified and modified[-1] == '.':
                    return modified[:-1] + 'dot'
                elif modified and modified[-1] == '@':
                    return modified[:-1] + 'at'
                return modified
        
        # Handle case where ends with 'dot' (but doesn't start with 'dot' or 'at')
        if s.endswith('dot') and length > 2 and not s.startswith('dot') and not s.startswith('at'):
            prefix = s[:-3]
            parts = prefix.split('dot')
            middle = '.'.join(parts)
            at_index = middle.find('at')
            if at_index != -1:
                new_mid = middle[:at_index] + '@' + middle[at_index+2:]
                return new_mid + 'dot'
        
        # Handle case where ends with 'at' (but doesn't start with 'dot' or 'at')
        if s.endswith('at') and length > 1 and not s.startswith('dot') and not s.startswith('at'):
            prefix = s[:-2]
            parts = prefix.split('dot')
            middle = '.'.join(parts)
            at_index = middle.find('at')
            if at_index != -1:
                new_mid = middle[:at_index] + '@' + middle[at_index+2:]
                return new_mid + 'at'
        
        return s
    else:
        parts = s.split('dot')
        middle = '.'.join(parts)
        at_index = middle.find('at')
        if at_index != -1:
            return middle[:at_index] + '@' + middle[at_index+2:]
        return middle

import bisect
n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
left_sums = []
for mask in range(1 << (n // 2 + n % 2)):
    total = 0
    temp = mask
    for idx in range(20):
        if temp & 1:
            total += a[idx]
        temp >>= 1
    left_sums.append(total % m)
left_sums.sort()

result = 0
for mask in range(1 << (n // 2)):
    total = 0
    temp = mask
    for idx in range(20):
        if temp & 1:
            total += a[(n // 2 + n % 2) + idx]
        temp >>= 1
    total %= m
    complement = m - total - 1
    pos = bisect.bisect_left(left_sums, complement)
    candidate = left_sums[-1]
    if pos < len(left_sums):
        if left_sums[pos] > complement:
            if pos > 0:
                candidate = left_sums[pos - 1]
        else:
            candidate = left_sums[pos]
    result = max(result, (total + candidate) % m, (total + left_sums[-1]) % m)
print(result % m)

import bisect

def generate_left_sums(arr, length, mod):
    sums = []
    def backtrack(idx, current):
        if idx == length:
            sums.append(current % mod)
        else:
            backtrack(idx + 1, current + arr[idx])
            backtrack(idx + 1, current)
    backtrack(0, 0)
    return sums

def generate_right_sums(arr, start, length, mod):
    sums = []
    def backtrack(idx, current):
        if idx == length:
            sums.append(current % mod)
        else:
            backtrack(idx + 1, current + arr[idx])
            backtrack(idx + 1, current)
    backtrack(start, 0)
    return sums

def egcd(a, b):
    r0, r1 = a, b
    s0, s1 = 1, 0
    t0, t1 = 0, 1
    while r1:
        q = r0 // r1
        r0, r1 = r1, r0 - q * r1
        s0, s1 = s1, s0 - q * s1
        t0, t1 = t1, t0 - q * t1
    return r0, s0

def tf(n, M):
    C = [0] * (n + 1)
    C[n] = 1
    for k in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        C[k] = (C[k + 1] * (k + 1)) % M
        if C[k] == 0:
            break
    return C

def app(n, M):
    K = [[[1]]]
    for i in range(n - 1):
        Ki = K[i]
        ni = len(Ki)
        Ki_ = [[0] * (i + 2) for _ in range(ni + i + 1)]
        K.append(Ki_)
        for j, Kij in enumerate(Ki):
            for k, v in enumerate(Kij):
                for h in range(i + 1):
                    Ki_[j + h][k] = (Ki_[j + h][k] + v) % M
                Ki_[j + i + 1][i + 1] = (Ki_[j + i + 1][i + 1] + v) % M

    C = tf(n, M)
    s = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        Ki = K[i]
        ni = len(Ki)
        mi = len(Ki[0])
        Si = [[None] * mi for _ in range(ni)]
        for j in range(ni):
            Si[j][mi - 1] = Ki[j][mi - 1]
            for k in range(mi - 2, -1, -1):
                Si[j][k] = (Ki[j][k] + Si[j][k + 1]) % M
        for j in range(1, ni):

                Si[j][k] = (Si[j][k] + Si[j - 1][k]) % M

        si = 0
        for j in range(1, ni):
            for k in range(mi - 1):
                si = (si + (Ki[j][k] * Si[j - 1][k + 1]) % M) % M

        c = C[i + 1]
        si = (si * c) % M

    n, mod = map(int, input().split())
    m = n * (n - 1) // 2
    
    # Using dictionary-based DP to avoid sparse array allocation
    dp = [dict() for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp1 = [dict() for _ in range(n + 1)]
    
    dp[1][m] = 1
    
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        # Calculate valid range bounds
        low_bound = m - (i - 1) * (i - 2) // 2
        high_bound = m + (i - 1) * (i - 2) // 2
        
        for x in range(low_bound, high_bound + 1):
            if x not in dp[i-1]:
                continue
            base_val = dp[i-1][x]
            for d in range(-i + 1, i):
                new_val = (dp[i].get(x + d, 0) + base_val * (i - abs(d))) % mod
                dp[i][x + d] = new_val
    
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        low_bound = m - (i - 1) * (i - 2) // 2
        high_bound = m + (i - 1) * (i - 2) // 2
        
        # First loop: multiply previous dp1 by i
        for x in range(low_bound, high_bound + 1):
            if x in dp1[i-1]:
                dp1[i][x] = (dp1[i-1][x] * i) % mod

    result = 0

    if n % 2 == 0 and m % 2 == 0:

problem_description.description: In one very old text file there was written Great Wisdom. This Wisdom was so Great that nobody could decipher it, even Phong — the oldest among the inhabitants of Mainframe. But still he managed to get some information from there. For example, he managed to learn that User launches games for pleasure — and then terrible Game Cubes fall down on the city, bringing death to those modules, who cannot win the game...For sure, as guard Bob appeared in Mainframe many modules stopped fearing Game Cubes. Because Bob (as he is alive yet) has never been defeated by User, and he always meddles with Game Cubes, because he is programmed to this.However, unpleasant situations can happen, when a Game Cube falls down on Lost Angles. Because there lives a nasty virus — Hexadecimal, who is... mmm... very strange. And she likes to play very much. So, willy-nilly, Bob has to play with her first, and then with User.This time Hexadecimal invented the following entertainment: Bob has to leap over binary search trees with n nodes. We should remind you that a binary search tree is a binary tree, each node has a distinct key, for each node the following is true: the left sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key, the right sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key. All the keys are different positive integer numbers from 1 to n. Each node of such a tree can have up to two children, or have no children at all (in the case when a node is a leaf).In Hexadecimal's game all the trees are different, but the height of each is not lower than h. In this problem «height» stands for the maximum amount of nodes on the way from the root to the remotest leaf, the root node and the leaf itself included. When Bob leaps over a tree, it disappears. Bob gets the access to a Cube, when there are no trees left. He knows how many trees he will have to leap over in the worst case. And you?

problem_description.description: In one very old text file there was written Great Wisdom. This Wisdom was so Great that nobody could decipher it, even Phong — the oldest among the inhabitants of Mainframe. But still he managed to get some information from there. For example, he managed to learn that User launches games for pleasure — and then terrible Game Cubes fall down on the city, bringing death to those modules, who cannot win the game...For sure, as guard Bob appeared in Mainframe many modules stopped fearing Game Cubes. Because Bob (as he is alive yet) has never been defeated by User, and he always meddles with Game Cubes, because he is programmed to this.However, unpleasant situations can happen, when a Game Cube falls down on Lost Angles. Because there lives a nasty virus — Hexadecimal, who is... mmm... very strange. And she likes to play very much. So, willy-nilly, Bob has to play with her first, and then with User.This time Hexadecimal invented the following entertainment: Bob has to leap over binary search trees with n nodes. We should remind you that a binary search tree is a binary tree, each node has a distinct key, for each node the following is true: the left sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key, the right sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key. All the keys are different positive integer numbers from 1 to n. Each node of such a tree can have up to two children, or have no children at all (in the case when a node is a leaf).In Hexadecimal's game all the trees are different, but the height of each is not lower than h. In this problem «height» stands for the maximum amount of nodes on the way from the root to the remotest leaf, the root node and the leaf itself included. When Bob leaps over a tree, it disappears. Bob gets the access to a Cube, when there are no trees left. He knows how many trees he will have to leap over in the worst case. And you?
